literal: The Taizu, Emperor Daowu — taboo name Gui — was the eldest son's son of Emperor Zhaocheng and the son of Emperor Xianming.
idiomatic: Taizu, Emperor Daowu, bore the taboo name Gui. He was a grandson of Emperor Zhaocheng by the principal line and the son of Emperor Xianming.

literal: His mother was called Empress He of Xianming.
idiomatic: His mother was Empress He of Xianming.

literal: At first, because of migration, she traveled at Yunze; later she lay down to rest, dreamed the sun came forth inside the chamber, awoke and saw light from the window reaching heaven, and suddenly felt stirred.
idiomatic: During the migrations she had been traveling in Yunze. One day she lay down to sleep and dreamed the sun rose within her chamber; when she woke, light poured from the window to the sky, and she was seized by a sudden presentiment.

literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month in the thirty-fourth year of Jianguo, the Taizu was born north of Canhebo; that night again there was radiance.
idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month in the thirty-fourth year of Jianguo, the future Taizu was born north of Canhebo, and that night bright light shone again.

literal: Zhaocheng was greatly pleased; the host of officials offered congratulations; a general amnesty was proclaimed; announcement was made to the ancestors.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng rejoiced; his ministers celebrated; the realm was granted amnesty; and the birth was reported to the ancestral shrines.

literal: The nurse found the emperor's body weight twice that of ordinary infants; she alone marveled at it in secret.
idiomatic: His nurse found the infant twice as heavy as other children and kept her wonder to herself.

literal: The next year an elm grew at the pit where the afterbirth had been buried; afterward it became a forest.
idiomatic: The following year an elm sprouted where his afterbirth had been buried, and in time the saplings grew into a wood.

literal: Though young he could speak; his eyes had bright light; broad forehead and large ears; the multitude all regarded him as unusual.
idiomatic: He spoke while still a child; his eyes shone; his forehead was broad and his ears large, and all who saw him thought him extraordinary.

literal: At age six, Zhaocheng died.
idiomatic: When he was six, Emperor Zhaocheng died.

literal: Fu Jian sent generals to invade within the borders; they were about to move the emperor to Chang'an; afterward he escaped harm.
idiomatic: Fu Jian sent armies against the realm and planned to relocate the boy to Chang'an, but in the end he was spared.

literal: The account is in the biography of Yan Feng.
idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Yan Feng.

literal: Fu Jian's army having returned, the state's people scattered.
idiomatic: After Fu Jian's forces withdrew, the tribes of the state broke apart.

literal: Fu Jian had Liu Kuren and Liu Weichen separately take charge of state affairs.
idiomatic: Fu Jian set Liu Kuren and Liu Weichen to govern the tribes between them.

literal: The southern grandee Zhangsun Song and Yuan Ta and others all led the former people south to attach to Kuren; the emperor then turned and took refuge with the Dugu tribe.
idiomatic: Zhangsun Song, the southern chieftain, Yuan Ta, and others led the old followers south to Liu Kuren, while the future emperor withdrew to the Dugu tribe.

literal: Year 1: buried Emperor Zhaocheng at Jinling and built the imperial coffin palace; the wooden pegs all grew and became a forest.
idiomatic: In the first year Emperor Zhaocheng was buried at Jinling. While the imperial tomb was being built, every coffin peg put in the ground took root until a grove stood on the mound.

literal: Though the emperor was young and tender, he stood apart from the crowd.
idiomatic: Though still a child, he already carried himself apart from other boys.

literal: Kuren often told his sons: The emperor has the will to take all under Heaven; to raise again great enterprise and spread light on the ancestors — it must be this lord.
idiomatic: Liu Kuren often told his sons, "That boy intends to rule the world, restore our great undertaking, and glorify the ancestors. The throne will be his."

literal: Year 7, winter, tenth month, [1] Fu Jian was defeated at Huainan.
idiomatic: In the seventh year, in the tenth month of winter, [1] Fu Jian was defeated at Huainan.

literal: That month, Murong Wen and others killed Kuren; Kuren's younger brother Juan took charge of the state's tribes.
idiomatic: That same month Murong Wen and his party killed Liu Kuren, and Kuren's younger brother Juan assumed leadership of the tribes.

literal: Year 8: Murong Wei's younger brother Chong set himself up in rebellion.
idiomatic: In the eighth year Murong Chong, younger brother of Murong Wei, declared himself ruler in defiance of the court.

literal: Yao Chang styled himself Great Chanyu and Ten-Thousand-Year King of Qin.
idiomatic: Yao Chang took the titles Great Chanyu and King of Qin of the Ten Thousand Years.

literal: Murong Chui presumptively styled himself King of Yan.
idiomatic: Murong Chui presumptuously declared himself King of Yan.

literal: Year 9: Kuren's son Xian killed Juan and replaced him; then he plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: In the ninth year Liu Kuren's son Xian murdered Juan and seized his place, then began to plot treason against the emperor.

literal: The merchant Wang Ba knew of it; he trod on the emperor's foot in the crowd; the emperor then galloped back.
idiomatic: A trader named Wang Ba learned of the plot and, in the press of the crowd, stepped on the emperor's foot; the emperor understood and rode away at once.

literal: At that time the former grandee Liang Gaizi's son Liu Juan was Xian's chief plotter; he knew the whole plan and secretly sent a tribesman, Mu Chong, to ride and report.
idiomatic: Liu Juan, son of the former chieftain Liang Gaizi, was Xian's chief conspirator. He knew every detail and secretly sent Mu Chong of his following to gallop ahead with warning.

literal: The emperor then secretly allied with old ministers Zhangsun Jian, Yuan Ta, and others.
idiomatic: The emperor then bound his old supporters Zhangsun Jian, Yuan Ta, and the rest in a secret league.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: then he took refuge with the Helan tribe.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he withdrew to the Helan tribe.

literal: That day Xian indeed sent men seeking the emperor but did not reach him.
idiomatic: That very day Xian sent men to seize the emperor, but they arrived too late.

literal: The account is in the biography of the Empress Dowager Xianming.
idiomatic: The fuller story is told in the biography of the Empress Dowager Xianming.

literal: That year the Xianbei Qifu Guoren privately styled himself Great Chanyu.
idiomatic: That year the Xianbei leader Qifu Guoren privately took the title Great Chanyu.

literal: Fu Jian was killed by Yao Chang; his son Pi set himself up in rebellion.
idiomatic: Fu Jian was killed by Yao Chang, and his son Fu Pi declared himself emperor.

literal: Dengguo year 1, spring, first month, day wushen: the emperor assumed the kingship of Dai, worshipped Heaven, established the era name, and held a great assembly at Niuchuan.
idiomatic: In the first year of Dengguo, on the wushen day of the first month of spring, he took the throne as King of Dai, sacrificed to Heaven, proclaimed the new reign, and held a great gathering at Niuchuan.

literal: Again appointed Zhangsun Song as southern grandee and Shusun Puluo as northern grandee.
idiomatic: He reappointed Zhangsun Song as southern chieftain and Shusun Puluo as northern chieftain.

literal: Distributed ranks and ordered exploits — each had his grade.
idiomatic: He ranked the nobles and recorded their merits, assigning each his due reward.

literal: Second month: visited Shengle in Dingxiang.
idiomatic: In the second month he went to Shengle in Dingxiang.

literal: Let the people rest and assessed agriculture.
idiomatic: He gave the people respite from war and set them to farming.

literal: Third month: Liu Xian himself fled south from Shanyou to Mayi; his tribesman Nuzhen led his following to surrender.
idiomatic: In the third month Liu Xian fled south from Shanyou toward Mayi, while his kinsman Nuzhen brought their clans in submission.

literal: Summer, fourth month: changed title to Prince of Wei.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he changed his title to Prince of Wei.

literal: Fifth month: the imperial carriage went east to Lingshi.
idiomatic: In the fifth month the court traveled east to Lingshi.

literal: The chief of the Protect-Buddha Marquis tribe, Hou Chen, and the chief of the Yifu tribe, Dai Ti, rebelled and fled.
idiomatic: Hou Chen, chief of the Hubohou tribe, and Dai Ti, chief of the Yifu, rose in revolt and fled.

literal: The generals pursued them. The emperor said: "Hou Chen and the others for generations have performed their duties; though they have small faults, we should for the moment bear with them.
idiomatic: His officers asked leave to pursue them. The emperor said, "Hou Chen and his people have served for generations. Their offense is slight; for now we should endure it.

literal: Now at the founding, hearts are not yet one; the foolish and near at hand should indeed hesitate — not worth pursuing."
idiomatic: We are only beginning to build the state, and loyalty is not yet settled. The timid will hang back — there is no need to chase them."

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiyou: the imperial carriage returned to Shengle.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jiyou, the court returned to Shengle.

literal: Dai Ti again came with his tribe to surrender; after several tens of days he fled and ran to Liu Xian.
idiomatic: Dai Ti submitted again with his tribe, but within a fortnight he broke away and fled to Liu Xian.

literal: The emperor had his grandson Beijin take charge of the tribe in his stead.
idiomatic: The emperor set his grandson Beijin over Dai Ti's people.

literal: That month, Liu Xian's younger brother Feini led horsemen to plunder Nuzhen's tribe, [2] and afterward led them in to surrender.
idiomatic: That month Liu Xian's brother Feini raided Nuzhen's camp with cavalry, [2] then brought his own followers in to submit.

literal: Earlier, the emperor's uncle Kudou had been moved by Fu Jian to Chang'an; he followed Murong Yong, and Yong made him administrator of Xinxing.
idiomatic: Earlier the emperor's uncle Kudou had been relocated to Chang'an by Fu Jian. He later followed Murong Yong, who appointed him administrator of Xinxing.

literal: Eighth month: Liu Xian sent his younger brother Kangni to welcome Kudou, with troops following, coming to press the southern frontier.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Xian sent his brother Kangni to escort Kudou south at the head of an army that threatened the frontier.

literal: Thereupon the tribes were disturbed and men's hearts wavered.
idiomatic: At once the tribes stirred and loyalty wavered.

literal: At the emperor's side, Yu Huan and others, [3] with men of the tribes plotted rebellion to answer them.
idiomatic: Yu Huan and others close to the emperor [3] conspired with tribal leaders to join the rebels.

literal: The affair leaked out; five plotters were executed; the rest were not questioned.
idiomatic: The plot was discovered. Five ringleaders were put to death; the rest were not punished.

literal: The emperor, fearing internal trouble, then crossed north over the Yin Mountains and took refuge with the Helan tribe, blocking the mountains for security.
idiomatic: Fearing civil war, he crossed the Yin Mountains to the north, withdrew to the Helan tribe, and held the passes for defense.

literal: He sent the envoy An Tong and Zhangsun He as envoys to Murong Chui to request troops; Chui sent envoys with tribute and ordered his son Helin to lead foot and horse to follow An Tong and the others.
idiomatic: He dispatched An Tong and Zhangsun He to Murong Chui to ask for aid. Chui sent tribute in return and ordered his son Helin to march with infantry and cavalry in support.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Helin's army had not yet arrived when the enemy had already pressed forward; thereupon the northern grandee Shusun Puluo and thirteen others and various Wuhuan fled to Weichen.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, before Helin's troops arrived, the rebels were already closing in. Shusun Puluo, the northern chieftain, twelve other leaders, and many Wuhuan bands fled to Liu Weichen.

literal: The emperor moved from Nushan to Niuchuan, encamped south of the Yanshui, went out through Daigu, and joined Helin at Gaoliu; Kudou was greatly defeated.
idiomatic: The emperor withdrew from Nushan to Niuchuan, camped south of the Yanshui, marched out through Daigu, and met Helin at Gaoliu, where Kudou's forces were shattered.

literal: Kudou fled to Weichen; Weichen killed him; the emperor gathered in all his followers.
idiomatic: Kudou fled to Liu Weichen, who killed him; the emperor absorbed his entire following.

literal: Twelfth month: Murong Chui sent envoys with tribute, presenting the seal and cord of Western Chanyu and enfeoffing him as Prince of Shanggu.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Chui sent envoys with tribute, offering the seal of Western Chanyu and investing him as Prince of Shanggu.

literal: The emperor did not accept.
idiomatic: The emperor refused the honors.

literal: That year Murong Chui presumptively styled himself emperor at Zhongshan, taking the era name Great Yan.
idiomatic: That year Murong Chui declared himself emperor at Zhongshan under the title Great Yan.

literal: Fu Pi died; Fu Deng set himself up in Longdong.
idiomatic: Fu Pi died, and Fu Deng established himself in Longdong.

literal: Yao Chang styled himself emperor at Chang'an, taking the era name Great Qin.
idiomatic: Yao Chang proclaimed himself emperor at Chang'an under the title Great Qin.

literal: Murong Chong was killed by his subordinates.
idiomatic: Murong Chong was murdered by his own officers.

literal: Murong Yong set himself up in rebellion.
idiomatic: Murong Yong rose in rebellion and claimed the throne.

literal: Year 2, spring, first month: distributed rewards to meritorious ministers Zhangsun Song and seventy-two others, each according to rank.
idiomatic: In the second year, in the first month of spring, he rewarded Zhangsun Song and seventy-two other meritorious men, each in proportion to his service.

literal: Second month: the emperor visited Ningchuan.
idiomatic: In the second month the emperor went to Ningchuan.

literal: Summer, fifth month: sent the envoy An Tong to levy troops from Murong Chui; Chui sent his son Helin to lead the host to join him.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he sent An Tong to Murong Chui to raise troops; Chui sent Helin at the head of an army to rendezvous with him.

literal: Sixth month: the emperor personally campaigned against Liu Xian south of Mayi, pursued to Mize, greatly defeated him; Xian fled south to Murong Yong; all his tribes were taken.
idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor marched in person against Liu Xian south of Mayi, chased him to Mize, and routed him utterly. Xian fled south to Murong Yong, and the emperor absorbed every clan that had followed him.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: the emperor returned from the campaign against Xian.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he returned from the expedition against Liu Xian.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day guimao: visited Ruyuan; sent the outer-court grandee Wang Jian as envoy to Murong Chui.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the day guimao, he went to Ruyuan and dispatched Wang Jian, a senior minister of the outer court, as envoy to Murong Chui.

literal: Eleventh month: then visited Chicheng.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he proceeded to Chicheng.

literal: Twelfth month: toured Songmo; returned and visited Niuchuan.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month he toured Songmo, then returned to Niuchuan.

literal: Year 3, second month of spring: the emperor toured east.
idiomatic: In the third year, in the second month of spring, he made an eastern progress.

literal: Summer, fourth month: visited East Chicheng.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he went to East Chicheng.

literal: Fifth month, day guihai: northern expedition against the Kumo Xi.
idiomatic: On the guihai day of the fifth month he marched north against the Kumo Xi.

literal: Sixth month: greatly defeated them; captured mixed livestock of their four divisions numbering more than a hundred thousand; crossed the Ruoluo River.
idiomatic: In the sixth month he crushed them, seized more than a hundred thousand head of mixed herds from their four divisions, and crossed the Ruoluo River.

literal: Distributed rewards to officers and soldiers, each according to rank.
idiomatic: He rewarded officers and soldiers according to their merit.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen: the Kumo chief Juji gathered the scattered, [4] and by night attacked the traveling palace.
idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the seventh month of autumn, Juji, a Kumo chieftain, rallied the fugitives [4] and struck the imperial camp by night.

literal: He loosed cavalry to strike and pursue; all were killed.
idiomatic: The emperor sent horsemen in pursuit and wiped them out to the last man.

literal: That month the emperor returned to Chicheng.
idiomatic: That month he returned to Chicheng.

literal: Eighth month: sent Jiuyuan Prince Yuan Yi as envoy to Murong Chui.
idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent Prince Yuan Yi of Jiuyuan as envoy to Murong Chui.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Murong Chui sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Murong Chui sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Twelfth month, day xinmao: the imperial carriage campaigned west, reached Nüshui, attacked the Jieru tribe, greatly defeated them, and captured men and women and mixed livestock numbering more than a hundred thousand.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the twelfth month he marched west to the Nüshui, struck the Jieru tribe, broke them completely, and took more than a hundred thousand captives and mixed herds.

literal: That year Qifu Guoren died; his younger brother Qian'gui succeeded him and privately styled himself Prince of Henan.
idiomatic: That year Qifu Guoren died. His younger brother Qifu Qiangui succeeded him and privately took the title Prince of Henan.

literal: Year 4, spring, first month, day jiayin: raided the Gaoche tribes, greatly defeated them.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the jiayin day of the first month of spring, he raided the Gaoche tribes and routed them.

literal: Second month, day guisi: reached Nüshui and attacked the Chituolin tribe, greatly defeating them.
idiomatic: On the guisi day of the second month he reached the Nüshui and defeated the Chituolin tribe.

literal: Day wuxu: Herangan and his brothers led the tribes to the rescue; they met the great army; he struck them in reverse and drove them off.
idiomatic: On the wuxu day Herangan and his brothers marched to relieve the enemy, met the main force, and were beaten back in a counterattack.

literal: Summer, fourth month: on the march returned to Chicheng.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he returned to Chicheng on the march.

literal: Fifth month: Chenliu Prince Yuan Qian was sent as envoy to Murong Chui.
idiomatic: In the fifth month he sent Prince Yuan Qian of Chenliu as envoy to Murong Chui.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Chui sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Murong Chui again sent envoys with tribute.

literal: That year the Di leader Lü Guang styled himself Prince of the Three Rivers and sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That year the Di chieftain Lü Guang declared himself Prince of the Three Rivers and sent tribute to the court.

literal: Year 5, spring, third month, day jiashen: the emperor campaigned west, halted at Luhunhai, raided the Gaoche Yuanhe division, greatly defeated them, and captured living captives, horses, cattle, and sheep numbering more than two hundred thousand.
idiomatic: In the fifth year, on the jiashen day of the third month of spring, he marched west to Luhunhai, fell on the Gaoche Yuanhe division, shattered it, and took more than two hundred thousand people and animals.

literal: Murong Chui sent his son Helin to lead the host to join him.
idiomatic: Murong Chui sent Helin with an army to join the campaign.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingyin: on the march visited Yixinshan; with Helin attacked the Helan, Ketulin, and Kexi tribes, greatly defeating them.
idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the fourth month of summer he advanced to Yixinshan, and with Helin crushed the Helan, Ketulin, and Kexi tribes.

literal: Sixth month: returned and visited Niuchuan.
idiomatic: In the sixth month he returned to Niuchuan.

literal: Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi to raid the Helan tribe and besieged them.
idiomatic: Liu Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi to attack the Helan and besieged them.

literal: He Ne and others asked to surrender and reported their distress.
idiomatic: He Ne and the other Helan leaders begged to submit and sent word that they were hard pressed.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day bingzi: the emperor led troops to the rescue; reached Yangshan; Zhiligidi withdrew and fled.
idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the seventh month of autumn the emperor marched to relieve them. When he reached Yangshan, Zhiligidi broke off and fled.

literal: Eighth month: returned and visited Niuchuan.
idiomatic: In the eighth month he returned again to Niuchuan.

literal: Sent Prince Gu of Qin as envoy to Murong Chui.
idiomatic: He dispatched Prince Gu of Qin as envoy to Murong Chui.

literal: Ninth month, day renshen: attacked the Chinu tribe at Nangqu River, greatly defeating them.
idiomatic: On the renshen day of the ninth month he attacked the Chinu at the Nangqu River and defeated them utterly.
